\begin{sloppypar}\noindent\textbf{How to read this appendix.} Each row of \cref{tab:chg-blueprint} is one change to the
blueprint (\file{docs/roadmap/protocol-blueprint.md}), placed where it applies: the rows follow the
blueprint's own order, section by section (the headline and \enquote{For zkVM engineers}, the scope,
the contracts and the ledger, the pinned conventions row by row, the spine, Layers 0 to 13, the
acceptance tests, the interfaces, the boundaries, the ordering, how work is tracked, the
references), and a finding that touches passages in several sections has a row in each. The first
column names the passage by its section and its lines at leanerVM \code{b435631} (at \code{144c5aa}
every line after 51 is four higher; the lines were re-read at \code{b435631} for this table, and
where a dossier's line differs the table gives the right one). The second column says the change
in a sentence or two. It is a summary: the text that governs is the one the third column points
to, the register row (\code{R1} to \code{R140}, \cref{sec:reg}) and the finding box that gives the
passage as it stands, as proposed and the reason, or, where no box has been typeset, the section
of the dossier under \file{.claude/reports/blueprint-review/dossiers/}. The fourth column is the
classification the dossier gives, in one of four words: an error of the blueprint, a deliberate
deviation, a deviation forced by an upstream library, or documentation (stale, missing or
misplaced text that is no divergence from leanVM); where the dossier gives none, the column says
so. The last column is the severity of the strongest finding behind the row.\end{sloppypar}

\begin{sloppypar}Three kinds of change are not in \cref{tab:chg-blueprint}. Changes to the status, the tracker, the
hole comment, \file{docs/architecture.md}, \file{docs/leanvm-target.md} and the other documents
are in \cref{ch:documentation} and in the drafts of \cref{sec:docs-texts} (among them the status
rows \code{R38}, \code{R83}, \code{R94}, \code{R95}, \code{R97} and the attribution of
\code{R100}). Findings against leanVM's own sources, to be reported to leanVM or recorded in
\file{docs/leanvm-target.md} (\code{R105} to \code{R109}, \code{R111}, \code{R112}, \code{R116} to
\code{R118}), change nothing here. Changes to the code are in the shorter
\cref{tab:chg-code}, with the file and lines at \code{b435631} in place of the passage. The rows
that ask the owner to choose between alternatives are marked \textsf{[decision]}; the alternatives
and the review's recommendation are in \cref{sec:chg-decisions}. The register's positions \code{R3}
and \code{R8} and its rows that propose no change to the blueprint (\code{R101}, \code{R104},
\code{R110}, \code{R113}, \code{R115}, \code{R123}, \code{R126}, \code{R133}, \code{R134},
\code{R136}, \code{R140}) appear only where they bear on a row.\end{sloppypar}

\multicolumn{5}{@{}l}{\textsf{\bfseries Pinned conventions (\code{:308-335}), row by row}}\\*
Row \emph{Sumcheck messages}, \code{:315} &
The oracle protocol sends four coefficients and checks the round, the wire three and none. Either
the wire's message becomes the oracle protocol's (three coefficients, the fourth derived, no round
check), or the row stays and Layer 4 proves the transport lemma (a verifier composed with an
injective decoding of wire messages onto the messages passing its round check keeps its
round-by-round knowledge soundness), Fiat--Shamir then taking a challenge oracle on the encoded
message. \textsf{[decision]} &
\code{R53}; \cref{f:table-pub-round-message} &
deliberate deviation (it owes a lemma the blueprint does not state) & \sev{minor}\\
Row \emph{Statements and parameters}, \code{:316} &
Add: the sizes are the prover's; the non-interactive theorem is stated for the family, its error
\lean{niError Q} the maximum over admissible sizes (or the sum, if the interface is per instance),
and \lean{FiatShamirSecurity} is the family form, the challenge oracle taking the announced sizes
with the statement. (A union over the admissible sizes costs about $2^{34}$, a hand estimate.) &
\code{R6}; \file{boundary-adaptor.md} §G.6 &
error of the blueprint (a missing decision) & \sev{major}\\
Row \emph{The oracle}, \code{:317} &
The stack's oracle interface is the inner product: a query is a \lean{Weight μ_stack}
(specification Definition 3.13), the answer $\sum_w W(w)\,q(w)$; an evaluation is the query
\lean{eqWeight r}. \textsf{[decision]} &
\code{R18}; \file{gt-opening-compile.md} §I.1, §A.5 &
error of the blueprint (caused by Layer 0's evaluation interface) & \sev{major}\\
Row \emph{The oracle}, \code{:317} &
Add: no phase before the opening queries the stack, and the opening queries it once (under the
inner-product interface); the compilation depends on it (see the spine's row on the
oracle-freeness of the front). \textsf{[decision]} &
\code{R138}; \file{obligations.md} §5.2 &
error of the blueprint (an omission in the design of the seams) & \sev{major}\\
Row \emph{Errors}, \code{:318} &
The spine fixes the closed form of every phase's error as a function \lean{piopError I} of the
instance's sizes, and \lean{Phases.Security} demands each phase's round-by-round bound at that
error; \lean{piop_rbrKnowledgeSoundness} is stated at \lean{piopError I} and \lean{piopError_le}
bounds its sum at the caps. A phase may not declare its own error: with an unconstrained
declaration the knowledge theorem holds of a protocol that checks nothing (declared error 1).
\textsf{[decision]} &
\code{R5}; \cref{f:code-spine-declared-error-unconstrained-knowledge-theorem} &
error of the blueprint (an omission the spine inherited) & \sev{major}\\
Row \emph{GKR}, \code{:321} (the layer sumcheck) &
\enquote{Layer sumcheck messages have degree 5 (eq × four multilinears)} becomes: the layer
sumcheck is normalized; the round message is the cofactor of degree 4 (four coefficients on the
wire, the constant one derived through the equality factor); the verifier checks
$(1 + r_t)\,h(0) + r_t\,h(1)$ against the running claim; the new claim is $h(χ_t)$; the layer's
final check has no equality factor. The table sumcheck is not normalized. (The register's position
\code{R8} kept $5/\abs{\E}$ per round: a loose upper bound; $4/\abs{\E}$ is tight.) &
\code{R7} (\code{R8}); \cref{f:bus-gkr-normalized} &
error of the blueprint & \sev{major}\\
Row \emph{GKR}, \code{:321} (the combiners) &
\enquote{A fresh combiner $λ$ per layer} becomes: a combiner is drawn after the roots and after
every layer, the last layer included; the last is used by nothing and its error is 0 (after
Fiat--Shamir it still changes every later challenge). &
\code{R9}; \cref{f:bus-extra-combiner} &
error of the blueprint & \sev{major}\\
A new row \emph{Leaf stacks}, after row \emph{Stacks} (\code{:322}) &
Per side, the boundary blocks of that side in the order of \lean{I.boundary} (state, memory,
bytecode), then each table's flushes of that side in order; the count side one block per count
column; stacked largest first at aligned offsets, ties by that index, no floor on the depth; the
depth of the three trees is the push side's. (The spine's \lean{tuples} lists the flushes first,
which is immaterial to \lean{Balanced} and a trap for the leaf layout.) &
\code{R50}; \cref{f:bus-leaf-order} &
error of the blueprint (omission of a transcribed convention) & \sev{minor}\\
Row \emph{Table sumcheck}, \code{:323} &
Prepend: the sumcheck ranges over the tables that have a constraint, a flush or a count column
(for leanISA the six opcode tables, never the tables of the shared columns); $τ_{\max}$ is the
largest log-height among them and the final message has one value per column of each. The
criterion is a decidable predicate of the spine (\lean{SumcheckTable} in the table-phase dossier;
\lean{M3Instance.active} in the boundary dossier, which puts the rule in row \emph{Statements and
parameters} or a new row \emph{Column groups}). &
\code{R11}; \cref{f:table-pub-sumcheck-tables}, \cref{f:bus-table-phase-tables};
\file{boundary-adaptor.md} §G.9 &
error of the blueprint (omission) & \sev{major}\\
Row \emph{Fiat--Shamir}, \code{:325} &
Every step is BLAKE2s-256$(cv \,\|\, \mathit{block})$ over 64 bytes, that is the RFC compression
$F(\mathit{paramIV}, cv \,\|\, \mathit{block}, t = 64, f_0 = 1)$ with the chain state in the
message, not the compression with $cv$ as chaining value; leanISA's \lean{compress} is $F$. (The
contract row \code{:216} and \lean{FsState.seed}, \code{:1203-1204}, are the dossier's evidence
for the same step.) &
\code{R66}; \file{gt-opening-compile.md} §I.14 &
none given (Category B wording) & \sev{minor}\\
Row \emph{Verifier shape}, \code{:326} &
Add: \lean{verify} takes a typed \lean{Program} and \lean{PublicInput}, so the deployed rejection

\section{Changes that depend on a decision of the owner}\label{sec:chg-decisions}

\begin{sloppypar}
The rows marked \textsf{[decision]} above, grouped by the choice they wait on. For each: the
alternatives the register or the dossiers offer, one line each, and the review's recommendation as
the register or the dossier gives it (where only the options chapter, \cref{ch:options}, gives one,
the entry says so). The other rows of the two tables do not depend on these choices, except in
wording.
\end{sloppypar}

\begin{enumerate}[leftmargin=*, itemsep=6pt]
\item \textbf{The oracle interface of the stack} (\code{R18}, with \code{R19}; rows in Scope, the
  row \emph{The oracle}, Layers 0, 10, 11 and 12).
  \begin{itemize}
  \item (i) Keep the evaluation oracle and the opening sumcheck, and owe a theorem relating that
    protocol to the deployed one.
  \item (ii) Give the stack the inner-product interface (a query is a weight, specification
    Definition 3.13); the opening phase is $λ$ and one weighted query, which WHIR realizes.
  \item (iii) End the oracle protocol at the Flock seam and let the compilation append WHIR.
  \end{itemize}
  Recommendation: (ii). (i) is rejected, since no implication exists between two protocols with
  different transcripts; (iii) is acceptable, but changes the master theorems' shape and leaves the
  stack's interface unused (\file{gt-opening-compile.md} §A.5).

\item \textbf{The shape of the bus seam} (\code{R2}, against the position \code{R3}; rows in the
  spine's sketch and prose, test 28, the code table).
  \begin{itemize}
  \item (a) \lean{BusOut} in the shape of the Rust's \code{BusVerify}: one point, forms per side and
    sumcheck table with the degree bound in the type, three totals, the column claims.
  \item (b) Keep the types and add the guards to \lean{Seam.bus} (at most $B + 3$ claims, one point
    per table, terms on sumcheck tables), checked by the table verifier and proved dead in the
    composition (Layer 12).
  \item (c) The smallest fix, for the degree only: \lean{VirtualTerm.poly} a subtype within
    \lean{I.d}.
  \item (d) No change beyond the bus phase's two side conditions: the seam's surplus burdens only
    the table phase (the position of \file{gt-bus.md}, \code{R3}).
  \end{itemize}
  Recommendation: (a), the table-phase dossier's redesign, which the spine dossier endorses
  (register \code{R2}; \cref{f:table-pub-bus-seam}). The second reading of the majors finds no
  tension between \code{R2} and \code{R3}: the bus phase fills its slot, and the table phase cannot
  serve the seam (\file{verify-majors.md}, summary).

\item \textbf{Which public-input check the phase models} (\code{R12}; the pooling of \code{R13} is
  needed either way).
  \begin{itemize}
  \item (a) Build the deployed phase (the combined equation on the two words, the values sent
    pooled) and let the master theorems and Layer 12 take it; keep the specification's per-limb
    phase as the reference, with the lemma that its acceptance implies the deployed one's; report
    the ambiguity of §8.2 to leanVM.
  \item (b) Keep only the specification's phase: the theorem is then about a verifier none of the
    three executable verifiers runs, and the debt assigned to Layer 12 cannot be paid there.
  \end{itemize}
  Recommendation: (a) (\cref{f:table-pub-public-input-check,f:code-pub-theorems-are-about-verifier-none}).

\item \textbf{Whether completeness carries an error} (\code{R4} against \code{R17}, with
  \code{R39}; rows \emph{Holes}, the spine's sketch, Layer 9, test 20).
  \begin{itemize}
  \item (a) A field \lean{err} in \lean{Component.Complete}, errors added by ArkLib's guarded
    completeness append, \lean{piop_completeness} with \lean{piop_perfectCompleteness} as its
    corollary, and a completeness error for the Flock phase (\file{lib-arklib.md} §G.2).
  \item (b) Perfect completeness stays: the specification's Flock is perfectly complete, the Lean
    honest prover sends the true coefficients, and the Rust prover's defect at $r_{\mathrm{eq}} = 1$
    is recorded in \file{docs/leanvm-target.md} (\file{gt-flock-ring.md} §8.4, §8.12).
  \item (c) Independently of (a) or (b): separate the guard from completeness
    (\lean{Component.Guarded}), so that knowledge soundness no longer presupposes completeness
    (\file{gt-flock-ring.md} §8.5).
  \end{itemize}
  Recommendation: the dossiers disagree. \file{gt-opening-compile.md} §E.5 agrees with (b) on the
  facts and calls (a)'s field \enquote{the right insurance}. The options chapter
  (\cref{sec:opt-recommendations}, item 5) recommends (c) with (b): completeness left perfect.

\item \textbf{Whether the framework stays on ArkLib's \lean{OracleReduction}} (\code{R34}; the
  ledger rows, Layer 10, the interfaces).
  \begin{itemize}
  \item (a) Stay on the framework ArkLib calls legacy, keep the port of \#615 until some ArkLib
    framework proves a guarded-first append, prove the plain corollary locally, and record the
    decision with its retirement condition.
  \item (b) Plan the migration to ArkLib's typed Interaction framework, which at \code{7653a901} has
    no knowledge soundness, no round-by-round notion and no extractor.
  \end{itemize}
  Recommendation: (a) (\cref{f:lib-legacy-framework}; the options chapter, item 9: nothing upstream
  is ready to receive the spine).

\item \textbf{How the phases' error is constrained} (\code{R5}; rows \emph{Errors}, item 6, Layer
  10, the code table).
  \begin{itemize}
  \item (a) A closed-form bound as a field of \lean{Phases.Security} (or a new \lean{Phases.Error}),
    the phases still declaring their errors.
  \item (b) The spine fixes each phase's error as a function \lean{piopError I} of the instance's
    sizes and demands each phase's round-by-round bound at it (the schedules then fixed by the
    spine too).
  \end{itemize}
  Recommendation: (b) (\cref{f:code-spine-declared-error-unconstrained-knowledge-theorem}).

\item \textbf{Where the error lives in the hole interfaces} (\code{R42}; row \emph{Holes}, the
  spine's sketch, the code table).
  \begin{itemize}
  \item (a) \lean{err} moves from \lean{Component.Def} into \lean{Security}.
  \item (b) The reduction becomes a computable structure that \lean{Def} extends.
  \end{itemize}
  Recommendation: the dossier gives the reason for (a) (the error is a property of the soundness
  proof, not of the reduction) without ranking the two (\cref{f:lib-err-noncomputable}); the design
  recommended in item 6 also takes \lean{err} out of \lean{Def}.

\item \textbf{The program hypothesis of the base theorems} (\code{R27}; the leanISA contract row,
  Layer 13).
  \begin{itemize}
  \item (a) Both theorems take \lean{hwf : WellFormedBytecode prog}.
  \item (b) \lean{verify} decides the program condition on the public program and rejects
    otherwise, which removes the hypothesis from the soundness theorem.
  \end{itemize}
  Recommendation: none; the register calls it a technical decision. The drafted texts of both
  dossiers take (a) (\cref{f:docs-base-theorem-hypothesis}; \file{boundary-adaptor.md} §G.3).

\item \textbf{The resources of base completeness} (\code{R29}, \code{R122}; Layer 13, the
  boundary with leanISA).
  \begin{itemize}
  \item (a) The completeness theorem from an execution takes a fit hypothesis \lean{hfit}, which is
    then the resource condition \file{architecture.md} asks for.
  \item (b) The leanISA roadmap supplies a \lean{constraintCompleteness} that returns a witness of
    minimal heights (itself needing a resource hypothesis, \code{R122}).
  \end{itemize}
  Recommendation: none given (\file{boundary-adaptor.md} §G.4 offers both).

\item \textbf{The round message of the sumchecks} (\code{R53}; row \emph{Sumcheck messages}).
  \begin{itemize}
  \item (a) The wire's message becomes the oracle protocol's (three coefficients, no round
    check): the compilation is literal and one check leaves the audit.
  \item (b) The oracle protocol keeps four coefficients and the round check, and Layer 4 proves
    the transport lemma.
  \end{itemize}
  Recommendation: the dossier does not rank them (\cref{f:table-pub-round-message}); the options
  chapter (\cref{sec:opt-tradeoff}) keeps the deviation, that is (b), with the lemma owed.

\item \textbf{The GKR inside the bus phase} (\code{R10}; the ledger row on context lifting,
  Layers 5 and 6).
  \begin{itemize}
  \item (a) Layer 5's GKR over a context, with the leaf tables derived from the stack and the
    zerocheck riding along; retired when ArkLib proves its lifting theorems and offers riders.
  \item (b) ArkLib's context lifting, whose completeness and knowledge-soundness theorems are
    admitted at both pins, and which alone would not carry the zerocheck clause.
  \item (c) A monolithic bus phase (named by the options chapter, item 6, not by a dossier).
  \end{itemize}
  Recommendation: (a) (\cref{f:bus-generic-gkr}).

\item \textbf{Where the Flock slot map and the adaptor's Flock obligations live} (\code{R15},
  \code{R16}; Layers 3 and 9, the interfaces, the boundaries).
  \begin{itemize}
  \item (a) \lean{blake2sLimbSlot : Fin 18 → Fin 256} in \file{Parameters/}, the low-index
    selection generic, Layer 3 building the reader, \lean{limbColumns} deleted
    (\cref{f:flock-ring-slot-map-circular}).
  \item (b) One instance-free \lean{FlockSpec}, supplied by \#3, with the slot map, the predicate,
    the lemma \enquote{R1CS $⇒$ compress}, the generator and its lemma; \lean{FlockWitnessGen} and
    \lean{limbColumns} deleted; the phase takes the \lean{FlockRegion I} of \code{R16}
    (\file{boundary-adaptor.md} §G.7).
  \end{itemize}
  Recommendation: none ranked; the register merges them into one change (\code{R15}), and (b)
  includes (a)'s slot map with the two obligations (a) leaves without a carrier.

\item \textbf{The bus phase's two side conditions} (\code{R43}; the spine's sketch, test 28).
  Fields \lean{one_le_d} and \lean{constrained_on_bus} of \lean{M3Instance}, or the same as
  hypotheses of the bus phase in Layer 6. Recommendation: none given (\cref{f:bus-side-conditions}).

\item \textbf{How the front's oracle-freeness is enforced} (\code{R138}; row \emph{The oracle},
  the spine, Layer 12, the code table).
  \begin{itemize}
  \item (a) A field of \lean{Phases} (or a hypothesis of the compilation theorem) that no front
    phase's verifier queries the stack, inhabited by the two built phases.
  \item (b) Front phases typed as plain verifiers lifted by \lean{keepOracles}, so that a query is
    a typing error.
  \end{itemize}
  Recommendation: none ranked (\file{obligations.md} §5.2).

\item \textbf{The error over the prover's announced sizes} (\code{R6}; row \emph{Statements and
  parameters}, Layer 12, test 21). The maximum over admissible sizes, with
  \lean{FiatShamirSecurity} in family form and the sizes in the challenge oracle's input; or the
  sum, if the interface is per instance (a union over about $2^{34}$ sizes, a hand estimate).
  Recommendation: the family form with the maximum (\file{boundary-adaptor.md} §G.6).

\item \textbf{The Merkle trees} (\code{R77}; the ledger, Layer 11). Build Layer 11 on VCVio's
  Merkle-tree library (VCVio issue 571), or write the trees here as planned. Recommendation: none;
  whether VCVio's trees fit leanVM's (BLAKE2s, the leaf encoding, pruned paths) is unverified
  (\cref{f:docs-vcvio-merkle}).

\item \textbf{The obligations no hole owns} (\code{R137}; the holes table, the ordering). One new
  hole per obligation, or each folded into the nearest hole with one new hole for the list-binding
  compilation. Recommendation: none ranked; \file{obligations.md} §5.1 gives the folding in full.
\end{enumerate}
